request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Medical Record Number: [REDACTED]
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]
Length of Stay: [REDACTED]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for chest pain and dyspnea on exertion of one-day duration. Initial evaluation with electrocardiogram and left heart catheterization revealed a diagnosis of anterior wall ST segment elevation MI, with 50% stenosis of the proximal LAD, 100% occluded mid LAD with thrombus in place, and 30% in-stent restenosis in the distal LAD. The patient underwent successful drug-eluting stent placement in the mid LAD.

The patient's hospital course was complicated by cardiogenic shock approximately 48 hours following the procedure, requiring intravenous diuresis and inotrope support. The patient was evaluated for advanced heart failure therapies, underwent a thorough evaluation, and planning for LVAD placement with periprocedural anticoagulation using bivalirudin was initiated. The patient was eventually discharged to a cardiac rehabilitation center.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Condition: The patient was discharged to a cardiac rehabilitation center with stable vital signs, improved hemodynamics, and without any significant complications.

Discharge Medications: [REDACTED]

Discharge Instructions: The patient was advised to closely follow up with the advanced heart failure clinic at our hospital and adhere to the prescribed medication regimen. The patient was also instructed to maintain a heart-healthy diet, avoid smoking and excessive alcohol intake, and engage in regular exercise as tolerated.

Follow-up: The patient will follow up periodically in the advanced heart failure clinic at our hospital.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is the anterior wall ST elevation myocardial infarction. It was established after investigation (ECG and catheterization) and was the condition chiefly responsible for the admission. The presenting chest pain and dyspnea are symptoms of the infarct, and the cardiogenic shock arose after admission, so it is a complication rather than the principal diagnosis.

In ICD-10-AM, acute STEMI of the anterior wall is I21.0 (acute transmural myocardial infarction of the anterior wall), which falls in the three-character category I21 (Acute myocardial infarction). The LAD involvement fits the anterior wall site.

The cardiogenic shock (R57.0) and the in-stent restenosis would be coded as additional diagnoses.

CODE: I21
